1. Read the two CSV files into pandas: one with the Q4-2022 NO₂ average for each of the 33 boroughs, the other a “neighbors” edge list.  
2. Merge the two so every borough row also contains a Python list of its neighbors.  
3. Missing-value rule:  
   • If the focal borough’s own NO₂ value is NaN, drop that borough entirely from all subsequent calculations; it will not appear in the hot/cold‐spot test nor in the data_points_used count.  
   • When building a local area’s total, ignore (skip) any neighbor whose NO₂ value is NaN; the sum is taken over whatever valid values remain.  
4. For every remaining borough i, build its local area set Sᵢ = {i plus all neighbors with non-missing data}. Compute the local sum Lᵢ = Σ(NO₂ values in Sᵢ).  
5. Collect the vector {Lᵢ}. Compute its mean μ and (sample) standard deviation σ.  
6. For each borough i, compute a z-score zᵢ = (Lᵢ − μ) / σ.  
7. Classify:  
   • HOT if zᵢ > 1.96 (95 % confidence) or 2.576 (99 % confidence).  
   • COLD if zᵢ < −1.96 (95 % confidence) or −2.576 (99 % confidence).  
8. Create a list of strings “BoroughName (HOT, z=<value>)” or “BoroughName (COLD, z=<value>)” for every statistically significant borough.  
9. Compute data_points_used = number of boroughs whose own NO₂ value was not missing (i.e., the length of the {Lᵢ} vector).  
10. Print:  
    print(f"data_points_used = {data_points_used}")

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load data
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
NO2_PATH = "chunks_csv/getisord/getisord_no2_Q4_2022.csv"
ADJACENCY_PATH = "chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv"

no2_df = pd.read_csv(NO2_PATH)            # columns: borough, avg_no2_value
adj_df = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)      # columns: borough, neighbor

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Remove boroughs whose own NO2 value is missing
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
no2_clean = no2_df.dropna(subset=["avg_no2_value"]).reset_index(drop=True)
valid_boroughs = set(no2_clean["borough"])

# keep only adjacency pairs where BOTH ends have valid data
adj_df = adj_df[adj_df["borough"].isin(valid_boroughs)]

# build neighbor lists ------------------------------------------------
neighbors_dict = (
    adj_df.groupby("borough")["neighbor"]
    .apply(list)
    .reindex(no2_clean["borough"])
    .apply(lambda x: x if isinstance(x, list) else [])
    .to_dict()
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Build local sums L_i (self + valid neighbors)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
local_sums = []
order = []                  # to remember borough order that matches local_sums

value_map = dict(zip(no2_clean["borough"], no2_clean["avg_no2_value"]))

for b in no2_clean["borough"]:
    neighs = neighbors_dict.get(b, [])
    # drop neighbors with missing own NO2 value (already excluded above)
    valid_neighs = [n for n in neighs if n in value_map]
    members = [b] + valid_neighs
    L_i = sum(value_map[m] for m in members)
    local_sums.append(L_i)
    order.append(b)

local_sums = np.array(local_sums)
mu = local_sums.mean()
sigma = local_sums.std(ddof=1)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Compute z-scores and classify
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
z_scores = (local_sums - mu) / sigma

results_list = []
for borough, z in zip(order, z_scores):
    if z > 1.96:
        results_list.append(f"{borough} (HOT, z-score = {z:.3f})")
    elif z < -1.96:
        results_list.append(f"{borough} (COLD, z-score = {z:.3f})")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Print required outputs
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
data_points_used = len(order)
print(f"data_points_used = {data_points_used}")

if results_list:
    print(f"FINAL ANSWER: {', '.join(results_list)}")
else:
    print("FINAL ANSWER: none")
